page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 12 vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 12.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data positions this instance in the average performance tier across most compute and memory metrics. The Intel Xeon CPU delivers a single-core stress-ng score of 1828.48 and a multi-core score of 11580.66, while Geekbench results show a single-core score of 1426.0 and a multi-core score of 7074.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 636.33 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 82.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 53.16 GB/sec for large-block writes. For specialized tasks, the instance achieves 11.77 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 13.6 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Large language model inference with a 7B parameter model is weak for prompt processing at 24.11 tokens/sec, but average for text generation at 10.83 tokens/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.u1-c1m1.3xlarge is its highly constrained memory capacity relative to its 12 vCPUs. With only 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, it is not suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. However, the dedicated CPU allocation and AVX/AVX512F instruction support make it a cost-efficient option for compute-heavy workloads that require parallel processing but have a small memory footprint. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded CPU-bound tasks, software compilation, lightweight web serving, and basic text or image processing.
description: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.3xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented server instance powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon processor. It features 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores, 12.0 GB of system memory, and a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no local storage or GPU accelerators. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it supports AVX and AVX512F instruction sets. Benchmarks indicate average performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7074.0 and a Redis SET throughput of 11.77 million operations per second. Due to its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core, this instance is highly specialized for compute-bound tasks with low memory footprints. It is best suited for parallelized CPU workloads, software compilation, and static web serving rather than memory-intensive database operations.
